chunks: He (peace be upon him) said: Verily, Allah, the Blessed and Exalted, when He created Adam (peace be upon him), He blew into him from His Spirit, so there was in him a single breath. When he died, that breath was taken, and it remained being blown into him and taken until the Spirit was expelled. Then they will be resurrected on the Day of Judgment.
ai.seo_question: What is the origin and nature of the soul according to this Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In *Kamal al-Din*, Shaykh al-Saduq contextualizes the divine breath (*nafkh al-ruh*) as the animating principle that distinguishes Adam’s creation, linking the physical expulsion of the soul at death to the metaphysical reality of resurrection. This narration underscores the Shia understanding of the soul's continuity and its dependence on Allah’s will, reinforcing the theological basis for bodily resurrection and the soul's journey beyond death.
